reason: I'd install it tonight, it's free and no admin needed, that's how I am. But one developer at 0.4.1 is exactly the kind of thing that's gone in a year, and my XnView MP does the browsing, batch convert and metadata in one place, so I won't make this the default.
why_switch_or_not: I'd try it for the fast next/back and the Space-bar preview from Explorer, and the gallery with batch rename/convert looks like it overlaps with what I use XnView for. But nothing in the description says it shows or edits metadata (EXIF/IPTC), which is half of why I keep XnView, and my files are phone photos, screenshots and PDFs, so RAW, 3D and the 26-format count don't matter to me. A speed gap of 40 ms vs a bit more on my own pictures is not something I'd notice.
current_app_pros: XnView MP is a browser, batch converter and metadata tool in one. It opens nearly everything I throw at it, it's free for home use, and I've used it for years so I know where everything is. It survives my yearly Windows reinstall because it's on my app list.
current_app_pains: It is a bit heavy and slowish to start up compared to a plain viewer, and the interface is cluttered with options I never touch. Nothing serious though, it does the job.
objection: One developer, version 0.4: will it still be maintained next year? If it stops, I've rearranged my default apps for nothing and I do that every Windows reinstall anyway.
would_change_my_mind: Seeing a year or more of regular releases and a public changelog, plus proof that it reads and edits EXIF/metadata like XnView does.
